extracted.intended_audience: general public, journalists, policymakers, and others researching the Sago Mine disaster and mine safety regulation
extracted.subtask_description: Compilation of regulatory, legislative, and best-practice criteria and requirements discussed in the Sago Mine disaster article — including MSHA rules, state rules, emergency temporary standards, legislative bill provisions, and journalism/FOIA practices arising from the incident.

rubrics_metrics.name: MSHA seal construction requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: MSHA rules seals to be built using "solid concrete blocks" or alternate materials that will withstand 20 pounds per square inch of pressure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page contrasts the MSHA 20 psi standard with use of foam 'Omega blocks' that state officials approved; NIOSH warned that without reliable seal designs miners' lives could be in jeopardy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition / moratorium on Omega (foam) blocks
rubrics_metrics.description: Following another accident where foam blocks failed, MSHA announced a moratorium on the use of Omega blocks and required testing for methane build up behind the seals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article notes state approvals that allowed foam blocks (which MSHA standards would not normally permit) and the later moratorium after a Kentucky accident; company claims about higher psi forces (60–90 psi) are noted but contrasted with NIOSH/ MSHA testing and guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of explosion-resistant ventilation seals (NIOSH guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: NIOSH reported that 'without reliable seal designs, miners' lives could be in jeopardy' and noted pumped cement seals (4 ft thick) tested and approved by MSHA 'effectively contained the explosion'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIOSH's report 'Protecting Coal Miners from Gob Explosions through Explosion-Resistant Mine Ventilation Seals (1993–2005)' is cited as recommending explosion-resistant seals and warning against unreliable/foam seals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Escapeways and refuges requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed clarification of existing standard 'Escapeways and Refuges' requires that a mine 'shall have two or more separate, properly maintained escapeways to the surface....'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article cites criticism that the administration rejected a clarification of this standard; the criterion emphasizes redundancy and maintenance of escape routes.

rubrics_metrics.name: SCSR availability (Emergency temporary standard)
rubrics_metrics.description: Self-contained self rescue devices (SCSRs): Provide additional SCSRs for each miner underground in a storage area to be readily accessible in an emergency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of MSHA's emergency temporary rules invoked to get proven technologies and techniques into the field quickly after the disaster.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lifelines in escape routes
rubrics_metrics.description: Install lifelines in all primary and alternate escape routes to help guide miners when visibility is poor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Included in the emergency temporary rules to improve miners' ability to find exits in low-visibility conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quarterly SCSR transfer training
rubrics_metrics.description: Miner training: quarterly emergency evacuation drills on transferring from one SCSR to another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MSHA's emergency temporary rules required more frequent, practical SCSR training to ensure miners can use and transfer devices under emergency conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rapid accident notification to MSHA (15 minutes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Accident Notification: informing MSHA of an accident within 15 minutes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the emergency temporary standard aimed at ensuring rapid federal awareness and response; related bills also mandate immediate operator notification with strong penalties for failure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Senator Byrd S.2231: communications, tracking, and air caches
rubrics_metrics.description: Bill would mandate equipment to communicate with miners, locate miners, and provide sufficient caches of air.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: S.2231's provisions are summarized as requiring communications/location equipment and adequate air caches; the bill was referred to committee and had multiple cosponsors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Senator Byrd S.2231: staffed rescue teams on site
rubrics_metrics.description: Rescue teams must be staffed and on site.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legislative proposal to ensure immediate, trained rescue capacity at mine incidents rather than relying solely on ad hoc responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Senator Byrd S.2231: operator notification penalties
rubrics_metrics.description: Operators must notify the MSHA immediately when there is an accident. Any coal operator who fails to do so will be subject to a $100,000 fine, and/or 12 to 15 years imprisonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The bill links timely notification to stiff criminal and civil penalties to deter concealment or delay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Senator Byrd S.2231: rapid notification and response system
rubrics_metrics.description: The bill would mandate a rapid notification and response system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A statutory requirement to coordinate and speed responses across agencies and operators following an accident.

rubrics_metrics.name: Senator Byrd S.2231: mandatory minimum penalty for negligence
rubrics_metrics.description: The bill would create a new mandatory minimum penalty of $10,000 for coal operators that show 'negligence or reckless disregard' for the safety standards of the Mine Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adds a specific minimum civil penalty tier to increase enforcement bite for reckless conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Senator Byrd S.2231: rescind/alter MSHA rule on belt-entry ventilation
rubrics_metrics.description: The bill would nullify an MSHA rule issued in 2004 that authorizes the use of belt entries for ventilation, which may have caused fire in another accident at Alma.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legislative intervention to reverse an agency rule seen as contributing to risk; demonstrates how statutory language can directly constrain regulatory technical choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Senator Byrd S.2231: science & technology transfer office
rubrics_metrics.description: The bill would create a science and technology transfer office in MSHA to pull research and development ideas from other federal agencies for use in the mines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutional recommendation to accelerate adoption of best-available technologies and cross-agency innovation into mine safety.

rubrics_metrics.name: Senator Byrd S.2231: ombudsman for miners
rubrics_metrics.description: The bill would create an ombudsman in the Labor Department's Inspector General office for miners to report safety violations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides an independent reporting and advocacy channel for miners to raise safety concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office of MHST: air cache quantity and placement rules
rubrics_metrics.description: State Office of MHST will require caches of air supplies to give each miner at least 16 additional devices. Mines with coal seams taller than four feet must have caches every 2,500 feet in each working section; in smaller mines, caches every 1,250 feet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operators must submit plans for cache locations within 30 days for review; however the rules set no deadline for equipping the mines with the caches (no immediate compliance deadline).

rubrics_metrics.name: Operators must demonstrate effort to acquire equipment
rubrics_metrics.description: Operators are expected to show they have the required equipment or that it's on order; if they cannot get them, they must show they have ordered them and are trying to get them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MHST director's statement acknowledges procurement backlogs and requires documentation of efforts rather than immediate physical presence of equipment where supply constraints exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mine and Industrial Accident Rapid Response System FOIA handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed rule requests filed under the state FOIA 'shall be held in abeyance until appropriate notification of next of kin of any deceased or victims that are grievously injured'. Next of kin must give consent for the release of information; FOIA requests must include 'exact dates and times' of accidents and 'the intended use of any information provided'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy to protect victims' families and control release of sensitive information; may be revised to balance FOIA responsiveness with notification responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to use 'proven technologies and techniques' in emergency temporary standard
rubrics_metrics.description: "This ... will require the use of proven technologies and techniques to help miners evacuate quickly and safely after a mine accident ... We are using the emergency temporary standard to get help into the field as fast as possible."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MSHA stated intent: emergency standards should rapidly mandate already-proven measures (e.g., SCSRs, lifelines) rather than untested innovations, to improve near-term safety.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journalism verification and ethical reporting standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists covering the incident were criticized for reporting unconfirmed survivor information; forum moderators and reporters emphasized verification: 'Get confirmation. Get confirmation', and that journalism 'is supposed to be a service to communities' and should avoid making victims 'the epicenter of a news event'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article records media lessons: verify sources before broadcasting, be cautious of scanner/local rumor sources, avoid sensationalizing victims' experiences; these are practical ethical criteria for coverage of tragedies.
